3923e47ce18d: Я люблю́ спорт, му́зыку и компью́терные и́гры.
ccce114436dc: Some words came from English: спорт, му́зыку, компью́терные, бо́ксом. Others came from Polish: я из Украи́ны (z Ukrainy), я люблю́ (lubię), прия́тно (przyjemnie). You have two keys to Russian, not one.
824991dc475a: Small м and к look a little different from English m and k. Same sound. And кот is Polish kot — same word.

bcca657bf31c: 1. One syllable is strong — and not like in Polish. In Polish the stress is always on the second-to-last syllable. In Russian it can be anywhere: ма́ма · метро́ · до́ктор · молоко́. In learner books it is marked with ́ . Learn each word with its stress.
c18fc72297fe: хорошо́ → kha-ra-SHO · молоко́ → ma-la-KO (milk) · соба́ка → sa-BA-ka (dog)
17ae60ccd33d: Polish never does this, so don't read Russian O the Polish way. Unstressed е and я get lighter too, close to ee: телефо́н → tee-lee-FON.
cfa02db04d6b: 4. At the end of a word, some letters go quiet — exactly like in Polish. б → p · д → t · г → k · в → f · з → s · ж → sh
